I am 52 years old and have farmed this land for 30 years. I only went to primary school, so I do not read many books or pamphlets — I watch what my neighbors do and remember what happened on my own fields. My family has seven mouths to feed, and some of my children work off-farm in the city, which brings in a little cash, but we are still careful with every yuan. I have 8 mu total and a well for irrigation, but pumping costs electricity, so I count every drop.

My backbone is the wheat-maize rotation on 5 mu. I plant wheat in October because that is what everyone in Quzhou does — it is our insurance crop. I buy improved wheat seed from the shop in town, about 30 jin per mu. Before planting, I run the rotary tiller over the field and spread about 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as my base. In spring, if the wheat looks yellow at jointing, I topdress with another 40 jin of urea. I irrigate three times: once before winter to protect the seedlings, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I spray herbicide once and insecticide twice — aphids and rust come every year. I expect about 1,000 jin per mu if the weather holds.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June. There is almost no time to turn the soil, so I no-till plant directly into the wheat stubble. I use hybrid seed — one small package per mu. I put down a little compound fertilizer at planting, about 60 jin per mu, because the wheat took a lot out of the soil. I irrigate twice if the rains do not come, and I spray for weeds and corn borers three times total. I hope for 1,100 jin per mu.

I keep 2 mu for cotton. Cotton prices have been okay lately, and my sister-in-law helps with picking. I rotary till in April and plant improved cotton seed. I use about 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as a base, and I topdress once. Cotton needs a lot of spraying — I do about 14 times for bollworms, aphids, and weeds. I irrigate twice, once at flowering and once at boll stage. I expect about 550 jin of seed cotton per mu.

The last mu I plant watermelon. My neighbor did well with watermelon last year, so I am trying it on a small plot to see if I can get some extra cash. I till with the rotary and plant hybrid watermelon seedlings. Watermelon needs more water, so I irrigate four times, and I put down extra potassium — about 90 jin of compound per mu plus a bit of extra potash. I spray for diseases and insects about six times. If it goes well I can get 7,000 jin per mu, which sells for good money at the market.

I thought about putting more fertilizer on everything, but fertilizer is expensive this year and my grandson needs money for school fees. So I will stick to what I know works and not gamble. I would rather apply a little too much than too little — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps — but I cannot afford to waste money either.
